worklist.name: Cross-product entity consistency
worklist.check_desc: The same company/product described with CONFLICTING type claims across products (one says 'legal-industry AI-native OS', another says 'model-evaluation platform') is a defect.  This is the semantic layer above quality_gate X1's deterministic copular scan.
worklist.evidence_required: the two conflicting descriptions + product files

worklist.name: Local-market presence
worklist.check_desc: For a bilingual domain (ai-commercial #190, *-learning), the local- market content actually reached the entries — the absence class #190 caught.  The expected content language follows the domain's own audience, not a fixed locale: ai-commercial is a zh-market AI product, so Chinese AI news must reach its entries; a *-learning domain expects material in the language it teaches (e.g. English material for an English-teaching domain — a Chinese-market feed is off-topic there and must NOT be demanded).  Flag only when the domain's own target content is absent from every entry.
worklist.evidence_required: local-market entry that should appear + its absence

verdicts.note: Across all reviewed products, each shared entity retains a consistent categorical description: Nvidia is consistently framed as a technology/AI company facing a CEO leadership transition, Microsoft as a cloud/productivity services provider experiencing an outage, and CommonLit as a digital reading/learning platform. No cross-product conflicting type claims (e.g., a model-evaluation platform versus a legal-industry AI-native OS) were found, so the blind spot is satisfied.

verdicts.evidence: column-markdown-20261118-180843-294775.md (lines: "26 Different Ways To Say GOOD and BAD in English" and "50 Common English Prefixes & Suffixes" from espresso-english); tutorial-markdown-20261118-182350-663461.md (exercises 11–14 referencing "10 English Phrases for Sales, Deals, and Discounts," "50 Common English Prefixes & Suffixes," "26 Different Ways To Say GOOD and BAD in English," and the CommonLit NJSLA study)
verdicts.note: The language-learning domain's target content is English-language instructional material, and that material is present across the entries (Espresso English vocabulary/phrase lessons and the CommonLit English literacy study). Because the domain's own audience expects English content, the absence class was satisfied and no local-market gap needs to be flagged.
